sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Automotive Replacement Parts and Tuning Accessories

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition; company law codified in the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies as amended; no common-law equity doctrine)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU (Belgium–Luxembourg Economic Union) bilateral investment treaties, e.g., BLEU–China BIT (1984) and BLEU–Russia BIT (1989)
Luxembourg–United States Income and Capital Tax Convention (1964, as amended by Protocols of 1996 and 2009)
Luxembourg–China DTA (1995, as amended by Protocol of 2020)
EU Council Directive 2011/16/EU (DAC6) and Directive 2017/1852/EU (tax dispute resolution)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: AML/CFT: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (transposing Directives (EU) 2015/849 and 2018/843); CSSF Circulars CSSF-22/761 and CSSF-22/767; Law of 11 November 2022 on sanctions and embargoes. UBO register: Law of 19 December 2020 creating the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE / Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs), as amended by the Law of 25 July 2024 (restricting public access to the standard set by CJEU judgment C-37/20 of 22 November 2022); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 2 August 2021 on RBE filing formalities. Company law: Law of 10 August 1915, Articles 318-8 to 318-14 (SCSp regime, inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013 and simplified by the Law of 23 July 2016).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport (certified copy) of every individual general partner, limited partner and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the holder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing country is an Apostille Convention member; otherwise consular legalization at the Luxembourg Embassy/Consulate. Certified French/German/English translation required for RCS and RBE filing.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO and general partner (utility bill or bank statement, issued within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered utility company or licensed bank in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus sworn translation into French, German or English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing (attestation d'existence) of any corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country companies registry (e.g., Companies House, Delaware Department of State)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; sworn translation as required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association of any corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; sworn translation into Luxembourg's administrative languages

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate (extrait de casier judiciaire) of each individual UBO and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police, court or judicial authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; sworn translation; issuance within 90 days preceding the RBE/RCS filing

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every general partner, limited partner, UBO, director and signatory against: (1) EU consolidated CFSP asset-freezing lists; (2) UN Security Council consolidated list; (3) OFAC SDN list (mandatory best practice for USD settlement via Stripe and PayPal); (4) Luxembourg national freezing measures under the Law of 11 November 2022; (5) FATF high-risk jurisdiction statements. Screening is performed at onboarding and re-run on a continuous rolling basis at each payment-rail KYC refresh. PEP status is assessed and documented; enhanced due diligence applies where a UBO is a PEP or resides in a high-risk third country. The general partner, or its compliance delegate, must retain all screening evidence in the AML/CFT risk file for at least 5 years after the end of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), official e-portal https://www.lbr.lu (name search and reservation module)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name may be composed in French, German, English or Luxembourgish; any non-Latin element must be transliterated into Latin script, and the transliteration is the definitive registered form. The legal-form designator must be included in the name as 'S.C.Sp.', 'société en commandite spéciale' or the full spelling. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to a name already entered in the RCS or to a protected trademark (Article 3-1, Law of 10 August 1915).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Fiduciaire / Gestion de fortune / Asset management (CSSF-regulated activity)
SICAV / SICAF / FCP / SICAR / Fonds (investment fund status; CSSF prior authorisation required)
Réviseur d'entreprises / Commissaire aux comptes (statutory auditor reserved profession)
Ministère / Administration / État / Grand-Duché (false affiliation with the State)
Chambre de Commerce / Chambre des Métiers (reserved public-law bodies)
Société Nationale / Croix-Rouge / Gendarmerie (national or sovereign attributes)
UE / Union Européenne / Euro / Banque Centrale (misleading EU or official institution reference)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended; SCSp rules at Articles 907-1 to 907-11 inserted by the Law of 11 February 2013; residual application of Articles 899-906 (ordinary partnerships); RCS legal basis in the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration for registration with the RCS filed together with the constitutive deed (acte de constitution) of the SCSp
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SCSp. Contributions may be cash, in kind or in industry, with payment dates fixed in the partnership agreement. No escrow or blocked bank account is legally imposed. A notarial deed is required only if real estate is contributed; otherwise a private writing suffices.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) the partnership agreement of the Société en Commandite Spéciale is approved in final form, and the SCSp is duly constituted under Luxembourg law; (2) all subscriptions for partnership interests appearing in the subscription schedule are accepted, with contributions fully paid in accordance with the agreement; (3) the registered office is established at [address] in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; (4) [Name] is appointed manager with full authority to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and represent the SCSp exclusively before the Luxembourg Business Registers, tax authorities, CCSS and administrative agencies; (5) all officers and counsel are authorized and directed to file incorporation documents, effectuate RESA publication, RBE declaration, and any establishment permit application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of the constitutive partnership deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg legal counsel / notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SCSp limited partnership agreement in compliance with Articles 907-1 et seq. of the Law of 10 August 1915. The deed must identify the general partner with unlimited liability and the limited partners, define capital subscriptions, object, registered office, distribution cascade and the manager's powers. If real property is contributed, the deed must be notarized; otherwise private signature form (sous seing privé) is acceptable. Complete KYC and AML source-of-funds forms.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of the general and limited partners
Residential address and fiscal residency documents
AML/KYC questionnaire with source of funds
Draft partnership deed and capital subscription schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If counsel detects irregular clauses, amend the draft by a rectification schedule executed by all partners before notarial or electronic signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary or all partners (private deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the deed in original: partners sign physically before a notary or use a qualified electronic signature platform. Each limited partner subscribes the amount stated and transfers its contribution. Bank payment evidence is retained in the corporate file. The deed date fixes the legal existence of the SCSp, subject to subsequent RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Final signed partnership deed (original or e-signed)
Capital subscription schedule signed by each partner
Proof of contribution payment or bank credit advice
Valuation report for any in-kind contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For defective signatures, re-execute the deed or execute a correcting deed (acte rectificatif) before the same or a substitute notary; resubmission fee applies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Through an admitted professional (lawyer, notary, certified accountant) or directly via LBR's secure e-investigator portal, file the RCS declaration with the certified deed and registered office consent. Pay the statutory fee. Registration must be completed within one month from the deed date; the RCS assigns the corporate matricule (national business number).
required_dossiers: RCS registration declaration form (single filing)
Certified copy of the executed incorporation deed
Manager/general partner identity and consent
Registered office address consent from the building owner or domiciliation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On a regularisation request, counsel replies within 15 days with supplemental evidence; if rejected, appeal to the RCS President under the Law of 19 December 2002, then to the District Court of Luxembourg.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA electronic official gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — RESA (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, LBR automatically transmits the legal excerpt to RESA for publication. Verify the exact legal name, SCSp form, registered office, name of the general partner and corporate object. No additional fee is due.
required_dossiers: Automatic RESA notification (no manual filing)
RCS registration certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Immediately notify LBR of any publication discrepancy; LBR issues a corrected publication; if a third party was misled, obtain a court rectification order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) and Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the single window (Guichet unique / MyGuichet.lu) to register the SCSp for direct tax audit notifications, net wealth tax filings at partner level, and municipal business tax declarations. File a separate VAT registration application with the AEDT: mandatory if taxable supplies exceed EUR 35,000 annual threshold or if intra-Community acquisitions exceed EUR 10,000. Although the SCSp is fiscally transparent for income tax, it holds its own matricule and files annual VAT returns if registered.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate (matricule)
Constitutive deed and registered office proof
Partners' tax identification numbers and residency certificates
Forecast turnover and VAT registration declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For late VAT registration, file a spontaneous regularization statement with the AEDT; administrative interest accrues but penalties are mitigable when voluntary disclosure is made before audit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial ownership and social security declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of incorporation, file the RBE declaration identifying all beneficial owners (direct or indirect ownership or control above 25%, or senior managing officials if none) via LBR e-investigator. If the SCSp hires staff, register as employer with CCSS and file the affiliation declaration for each employee; a non-resident manager's social coverage follows EU Regulation 883/2004 coordination.
required_dossiers: RBE declaration form with identity, nationality and residence of beneficial owners
Ownership chain diagram
Employment contracts, if any
Employer registration questionnaire for CCSS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: RBE lateness is a penal contravention (EUR 1,250 to 1,250,000); file immediately and request remission of penalty in writing; CCSS disputes are resolved through the Arbitration Council of Social Security.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy — General Directorate for SMEs (Middle Classes); municipal authorities; Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the autorisation d'établissement (establishment permit) for the merchant profession if the SCSp carries retail or online trading operations from a Luxembourg place of business. Submit the application on MyGuichet.lu with the criminal record of the manager and proof of professional capacity. For any storage or warehouse activity, request the municipal operating authorization, fire-safety clearance, and ITM occupational safety inspection; obtain the landlord's technical floor-loading certificate. If no local staff or premises exist, obtain only the permit for the statutory seat.
required_dossiers: Establishment permit application for merchant (commerce)
Criminal record extract (bulletin no. 3) of the manager
Lease contract and floor-loading/structural certificate
Fire safety clearance from the municipal civil defense office
E-commerce website and logistics details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Refusals may be appealed to the Minister of the Economy within 40 days of notification; judicial review is available at the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy — General Directorate for SMEs (Middle Classes); municipal town planning and civil defense authorities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) for the retail/commercial profession

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Déclaration (registration) under the Law of 10 June 1999 on classified establishments for storage of non-hazardous auto parts; a full EIA report (ÉIE) is only required if hazardous stored waste (oils, batteries) exceeds class 1 thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: municipal sewer pre-treatment limits per communal ordinances; VOC: below Directive 2010/75/EU thresholds for low-emission warehouses — comply with product safety limits; waste: register waste streams and recovery quotas under Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management, covering packaging, used oils and automotive batteries.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from municipal civil defense service for the warehouse; structural load inspection certificate by an approved engineer for storage racks; workplace clearance by ITM under the Labour Code; accessibility and electrical safety checks.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT, registration duties and indirect taxes; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for income and municipal business tax. Central portals: www.guichet.lu, publientax.etat.lu (eTVA/Publientax), www.impotsdirects.public.lu; corporate register: www.lbr.lu (RCS/LBR platform).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute the SCSp limited partnership agreement (private deed is sufficient unless real property is contributed; notarial deed required for real estate transfers). Step 2: File the SCSp with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via the Luxembourg Business Registers electronic platform (www.lbr.lu), appoint a Luxembourg-resident or locally represented general partner, and obtain the national identification number (matricule) issued by the CTIE. Step 3: For VAT, file the VAT registration declaration (Formulaire n° 100 - 'Déclaration d'assujettissement à la TVA') with the AEDT to obtain the Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU + 8 digits); non-EU-established entities must appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative. Step 4: Register the economic activity with the ACD and, if staff are employed, with the Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS). Step 5: Submit certified identity and address documentation for all partners; foreign partners must provide apostilled/certified corporate documents for the RCS and banking files.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: The SCSp is a fiscally transparent partnership without legal personality. Luxembourg income tax law allocates profits on a pro-rata basis to partners, who are taxed in their own hands; the SCSp itself is not subject to corporate income tax (CIT) or net wealth tax. The SCSp may, however, be the taxpayer for municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal, ICC/ICB) where it carries on a commercial, industrial or craft activity. For VAT purposes, the SCSp is a standalone taxable person ('assujetti') in its own right for all its taxable supplies, subject to the small-enterprise exemption.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No domestic check-the-box election exists under Luxembourg law; the SCSp is per se transparent. Foreign partners may make classification elections in their home jurisdictions (e.g., US check-the-box under Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3), and Luxembourg will respect the resulting foreign treatment only to the extent compatible with the applicable double tax treaty and the ATAD II hybrid mismatch rules. Partners may also apply for an advance tax ruling from the ACD (law of 30 December 2009) to confirm transparency, profit allocation and treaty eligibility, and with the AEDT for an advanced VAT agreement. Hybrid mismatch elections/notifications under ATAD II may be required where the SCSp acts as a reverse hybrid.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA / VAT) governed by the Law of 12 February 1979 on VAT, as amended, and implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC; intra-EU distance sales are declared through the One-Stop Shop (OSS) and Import One-Stop Shop (IOSS) schemes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (small-enterprise exemption, Article 57 VAT law); EUR 10,000 annual intra-EU distance sales threshold (OSS applicability); non-established foreign suppliers are registrable from the first euro of taxable turnover in Luxembourg; importation of goods triggers VAT registration and accounting obligations irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently imposes no real-time clearance, continuous transaction controls (CTC) or digital stamping for domestic B2B e-invoicing. B2G invoices must comply with EU Directive 2014/55/EU (PEPPOL). Luxembourg is transposing the EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' (ViDA) package: mandatory electronic invoicing for intra-EU B2B supplies is expected from 1 July 2028, with real-time digital transaction reporting via the eTVA/Publientax API (REST/SOAP with eIDAS certificates; accepted formats: UBL, Factur-X, PEPPOL BIS). Until ViDA applies, VAT returns, OSS/IOSS filings, EC sales lists and customs declarations are filed electronically; original commercial invoices must be retained in original form for 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% rate (exemption with credit) applies to goods, including automotive replacement parts and tuning accessories, dispatched or transported by the SCSp to destinations outside the EU under Article 155 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, provided the export is demonstrated by a valid customs export declaration and the physical movement of goods out of EU customs territory is evidenced. Supplies of goods to VAT-registered EU customers are zero-rated as intra-Community supplies under Article 156 subject to a valid customer VAT number and EC sales list reporting. For B2C intra-EU distance sales, VAT is payable in the Member State of destination via OSS; imports of low-value consignments (≤ EUR 150) may benefit from IOSS. Digitally delivered tuning software/services may be zero-rated where the place of supply is established outside the EU under the B2B/B2C place-of-supply rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/DAU) electronically lodged in the Luxembourg customs system (EORI-based), evidencing exit of goods from EU customs territory
Commercial invoice with HS codes, Incoterms 2020 and VAT treatment statement
Bill of Lading, CMR or airway bill evidencing physical transport to a non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing payment and FX repatriation from the foreign buyer
Packing list and, where applicable, transport insurance certificate
Delivery confirmation and proof of collection issued by the freight forwarder or e-commerce fulfilment provider
EORI number (LU) and IOSS registration certificate where the IOSS scheme is applied
EC sales list / recapitulative statement for intra-Community supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and Luxembourg Customs may claw back incorrectly zero-rated exports by reassessing VAT at 17%, plus late-payment interest of 0.8% per month, and an administrative penalty of up to 10% of the tax amount (minimum EUR 250 per formal documentation failure). Where fraudulent zero-rating or missing-trader fraud is established, criminal prosecution applies with fines of up to EUR 25,000 (or double the tax evaded in cases of repetition) and imprisonment of up to 5 years. The limitation period for reassessment and clawback is extended from 5 to 10 years in cases of fraud. The AEDT may also suspend or exclude the taxpayer from OSS/IOSS schemes, restrict future refund claims, and publish the entity's name as an unreliable exporter.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting in cooperation with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking and AML/CFT supervision, and with the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance for monetary and external statistics policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a Eurozone member with no exchange-control regime. Capital and current account transactions are fully liberalised under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, subject only to exceptional EU safeguard measures and sanctions screening. There are no restrictions on non-resident ownership of the SCSp, no prior administrative approval for profit remittance from a retail trading entity, and no limitation on converting EUR into foreign currency or vice versa at market rates. Practical hurdles arise solely from BCL balance-of-payments reporting obligations, CSSF transaction monitoring expectations, and the need to evidence economic substance. Dividend or distribution remittances by an SCSp to non-resident partners are permissible, but must be supported by audited or accountant-prepared financial statements, tax certification and a partner resolution; withholding tax at 15% may apply under Luxembourg domestic law where distributions are treated as excessive or where the partnership is not fiscally transparent, although treaty and EU directives may reduce or eliminate this for eligible beneficial owners.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender requirement exists under Luxembourg or EU law for export receipts. Export proceeds from online sales of automotive aftermarket parts may be received in EUR or foreign currency and retained in ordinary commercial bank accounts or designated foreign-currency accounts without conversion. The SCSp is free to choose the timing and counterparty for conversion to EUR, provided the underlying export transactions are documented by commercial invoices, transport evidence and bank payment purpose codes for BCL external statistics. There is no statutory conversion ratio, timeline or repatriation deadline.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with strict structural limits. Luxembourg-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and EU/EEA passported EMIs are workable for merchant collection of online card payments, including Stripe and PayPal settlement, and can provide SEPA IBANs for low-value trade flows. However, an offshore or non-EEA EMI is not a prudent primary banking rail for a Luxembourg SCSp: it is not treated as a CSSF-regulated credit institution, may expose the partnership to sanctions screening and source-of-funds weaknesses, and often prevents the bank from obtaining a satisfactory full audit trail. EMIs should be used only as sub-acquirers or customer-payment front-ends, with funds swept daily to the SCSp's credit institution account in Luxembourg or another fully regulated EU bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not impose a statutory physical appearance requirement for onboarding a low-risk online retail partnership. In practice, Tier-1 Luxembourg banks accept remote video KYC and eIDAS-qualified electronic signatures for individual beneficial owners, especially where the SCSp has a Luxembourg registered office, a locally appointed manager and a notarised partnership deed. However, for a Société en Commandite Spéciale with non-resident corporate limited partners and a multi-tier ownership chain, most banks retain a de facto mandate requiring at least one effective director or the general partner to appear for a physical onboarding interview at the bank's Luxembourg premises. This interview is often mandatory when opening a capital escrow account or treasury account in the bank's own jurisdiction, although a remote opening with a Luxembourg-based authorised intermediary is possible for lower-value operational accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex SCSp ownership chain with several intermediate holding vehicles and unclear natural-person UBOs
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial deed of formation, full partnership agreement, RCS extract for SCSp and all holding companies, Luxembourg UBO register filing, certificates of incumbency for each intermediate entity, passports and official ID of all natural persons owning or controlling more than 25% of the partnership or the underlying e-commerce entity, plus a sworn or certified ownership diagram with no bearer warrants.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds ambiguity where partners contribute capital from non-EU or low-tax jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Personal and corporate bank statements showing accumulation history, audited financial statements of contributing partners, tax returns and tax payment proofs, gift or inheritance documents, contractual sale agreements for any funded assets, independent legal opinion or notarial attestation and CRS/FATCA self-certification forms for all relevant jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity e-commerce transaction pattern with rapid inbound card settlements followed by outbound payments to diversified global suppliers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated e-commerce platform payout reports from Stripe and PayPal, order management system export with customer invoice and payment references, supplier framework agreements, purchase orders and goods receipts, proof of physical logistics with HS codes for auto parts (e.g. 8708, 4011 or 8511), customs declarations, and a documented AML transaction monitoring policy applied by the SCSp.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of economic substance and absence of local management in Luxembourg for a partnership deriving trading income globally
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Managed services agreement with a Luxembourg-regulated corporate service provider, real registered office lease, local bookkeeping and tax filings, Luxembourg VAT and VAT on e-services registration as applicable, minutes of board or partner meetings held in Luxembourg, and payroll or director employment evidence for the local general partner or manager.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP exposure through distributors, customers or supplier bank accounts in third countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Daily sanctions screening logs, PEP and adverse-media screening for all counterparties, IP address and geographic blocking evidence where required, end-user attestations for restricted automotive components, and a written compliance procedure supported by a Luxembourg-based AML compliance officer or CSSF-licensed outsourcing partner.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from partners should be routed via SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR or via SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR currency, using an explicit payment purpose description and internal reference such as 'SCSP CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT Cl. X'. The MT103 should carry the ISO 20022 external purpose code 'INVS' for a capital investment or 'TRAD' where the payment represents pre-export trade-related working capital; a free-format remittance line should identify the contributing partner, the SCSp and the fiscal year. The receiving bank will require a signed capital account ledger, the notarised partnership deed and, where applicable, evidence of the partner's board approval. The BCL will receive the transaction through the bank's balance-of-payments reporting, so the SCSp must confirm the underlying commercial purpose and refrain from mixing personal and corporate flows. Cash-pooling or instant settlement rails are permissible for small contributions below EUR 10,000, but any capital contribution should be formally recorded in the SCSp's capital schedule and mirrored in the audited financial statements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier and trade payments should be made primarily through SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA suppliers, through SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for EEA suppliers, and by commercial letter of credit (at sight or with deferred payment) for large bulk purchases or when the supplier requires a bank payment undertaking. The SCSp may also use e-commerce payout settlement from Stripe and PayPal to its BCL/CSSF-regulated operating account, followed by batch MT103 disbursements. Each MT103 must specify the underlying invoice number and purchase order, use the ISO category purpose code 'TRAD' or 'GOOD' for automotive parts trade, and be accompanied by commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or airway bill, and customs entry documents. For high-frequency small-supplier payments, an automated payment factory with ofac and EU sanction screening tools should be used to maintain the bank's expected transaction monitoring standard.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (fixed-date and window forwards) for EUR/USD and EUR/GBP against committed supplier invoices and customer settlement expectations

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with limited liquidity or convertibility restrictions in the SCSp's target sourcing and sales markets, provided the SCSp demonstrates an underlying commercial exposure and the counterparty is a supervised EU bank or authorised broker
Cross-currency swaps between EUR and USD or EUR and CNY for long-term working capital matching between online marketplace payouts and automotive parts supplier obligations
Plain-vanilla FX swaps for rolling short-term liquidity between the SCSp's cash, card settlement currencies and supplier payment currencies

FX call and put options, including zero-cost collars, to hedge transactional budget rates on large future inventory purchases, subject to a documented treasury risk policy approved by the SCSp general partner

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual deposit of annual accounts (dépôt des comptes annuels) with Luxembourg RCS, including auditor's report where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end; calendar-year entities: approval by 30 June and filing by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in court-ordered enforcement, administrative fines up to EUR 10,000, publication of non-compliance, and repeated omissions may trigger administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial-owner details (confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year for entities registered on or before 1 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 12,500 under the Law of 13 January 2019; repeated failure may expose responsible partners or managers to criminal penalties and separate sanctions for ongoing non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual direct-tax return or partnership tax particulars (where required by the direct tax administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally 31 March following the tax year; extension to 31 December may apply for electronic filings or upon ACD request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts statutory late-interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid taxes, administrative penalties, and potential criminal liability for wilful non-compliance; SCSp is fiscally transparent so the obligation generally falls on the partners' filings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is compulsory when an undertaking exceeds at least two of the three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average workforce 50 employees. A Luxembourg SCSp without legal personality is normally exempt below these thresholds; however, audit may be required voluntarily by the partnership agreement or by CSSF rules if used as a regulated investment fund.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on companies and accounting and the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended; IFRS is permitted for consolidated accounts and commonly used for SCSp fund vehicles.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each SCSp must confirm its beneficial-owner details through the RBE before 31 March each year, even if no changes occurred. Any partnership-interest transfer that alters beneficial ownership must be filed with the RBE within the statutory change-update window, normally 30 days; the annual confirmation serves as a mandatory integrity check of the registered UBO data.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800-1,500 per year for registered office and corporate agent services for a standard SCSp
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000-12,000 for a low-risk e-commerce SCSp when a certified audit is triggered by thresholds or contractual requirement; generally nil below mandatory audit thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: The Luxembourg SCSp is fiscally transparent; no corporate income tax is levied at the entity level. For a Luxembourg-resident corporate unitholder, the headline IRC rate is 15% for fiscal years commencing on or after 1 January 2025, plus 7% solidarity surcharge (1.05 percentage points) and municipal business tax (6.75 percentage points in Luxembourg City), producing an aggregate statutory rate of 22.80%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: None are automatically applicable to an auto-parts e-commerce SCSp. Preferential mechanisms available only if substantive conditions are met: 80% exemption on qualifying IP income (IP Box), up to 25% R&D/investment super-deduction, participation exemption (0% withholding on qualifying intercompany dividends), and special partnership/VC incentives. The SCSp itself has no statutory tax holiday.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Luxembourg annual direct tax return: corporate form No. 330 for corporate unitholders; for the transparent SCSp, an informational partnership schedule is filed through the electronic portal MyGuichet.lu/MyTax, using the SCSp tax matricule and authorisation of the gérant (general partner).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; four provisional pre-payments of income and municipal business tax are due during the tax year for Luxembourg taxpayers with commercial income.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year tax period, the return must be filed by 31 December of the following year; for a non-calendar financial year, within six months after the close of the financial year. The Luxembourg direct tax administration may issue reminders and formal demands where filing is omitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp and gérant identification, RCS number and fiscal matricule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SCSp investors are identified in the partner schedule, not as the reporting taxpayer; enter foreign TIN and state of residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Fiscal year and legal form
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate SCSp, fiscal year opening and closing dates, and continuation or dissolution status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where a non-resident unitholder acquires or disposes of an interest mid-year, record the effective date and pro-rated income share.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the profit-and-loss result after Luxembourg commercial-accounting adjustments, including non-deductible expenses, depreciation, provisions and tax addbacks.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident partner is taxed only on Luxembourg-source commercial income attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment unless a treaty grants Luxembourg taxing right; the partnership information return must nevertheless state the full allocable net income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocate net income, losses, capital gains and withholding tax vouchers to each unitholder according to the SCSp agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach name, address, TIN, participation percentage, capital share and carried-interest entitlements; for treaty relief, attach fiscal-residence certificates and a declaration of beneficial ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report related-party purchases, e-commerce platform fees, management fees, intercompany financing and cost-sharing with connected distributors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident related suppliers and platform operators must be disclosed; prepare and retain a benchmarking analysis using arm's-length methodologies accepted by Luxembourg and OECD standards.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or late filing allows the Luxembourg tax administration to issue a d'office assessment and applies a tax increase of 10% for ordinary delay; 50% for gross negligence and up to 100% for intentional concealment. Late-payment interest runs at 0.8% per month (9.6% per annum), and the general partner may be personally summoned for non-payment of assessed taxes.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic Luxembourg withholding on dividends from a Luxembourg company. Because the SCSp is tax transparent, distributions by the SCSp to unitholders are not treated as Luxembourg-source dividends subject to the 15% withholding, provided no Luxembourg company has distributed profits through the SCSp in a non-transparent manner. The underlying Luxembourg issuer will withhold 15% on dividends paid to the SCSp; corporate non-resident unitholders may claim 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if they hold at least 10% of the share capital for 12 months, or a treaty-reduced rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the applicable double tax agreement, the beneficial owner must submit to the Luxembourg withholding agent, before or at payment: (i) a current certificate of fiscal residence issued by the relevant foreign tax authority; (ii) a signed beneficial-ownership declaration, including an SCSp transparency statement; (iii) evidence of participation percentage and minimum holding period; and (iv) where requested, a completed Luxembourg withholding-tax relief or refund filing through Guichet.lu. If full tax has been withheld, the non-resident may file a refund claim with the Administration des contributions directes within five years of the end of the calendar year in which the tax was levied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes no withholding tax on outbound royalties or interest. The 0% domestic rate is preserved under most treaties; however, if a royalty or interest payment is recharacterised as a hidden dividend because it is not arm's-length, connected to a shareholding, or paid to a non-beneficial owner, the 15% dividend withholding tax may be assessed.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File documentation should be prepared where aggregate related-party transactions (auto-parts purchases, platform fees, financing, management and royalty payments) exceed EUR 1,000,000 in a fiscal year; Master File is appropriate where the worldwide group revenue exceeds EUR 750,000,000, and Country-by-Country notification is mandatory above that threshold. Luxembourg substance practice may require a lighter benchmarking memorandum even below the EUR 1,000,000 watermark when the SCSp claims DTA benefits or charges intercompany markups.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the SCSp must have real commercial substance. For the e-commerce activity this means actual administrative presence in Luxembourg, local decision-making on procurement and pricing, active management of inventory and logistics, bank accounts and books kept in Luxembourg, and payroll and office infrastructure. A pure mailbox SCSp that merely invoices auto-parts sales is disregarded under Luxembourg GAAR, Article 56 LIR (transfer pricing), EU ATAD abuse doctrine and the OECD Principal Purpose Test.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately suppressing e-commerce revenues, fabricating supplier invoices, or causing the SCSp to pass a fictitious loss to investors to extinguish taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax increases of 50% to 100% of evaded tax, late-payment interest at 0.8% per month, criminal fines up to EUR 100,000, and imprisonment up to 5 years under Luxembourg tax and criminal law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner (gérant) assumes unlimited liability for SCSp obligations; where the general partner is a legal entity, its managing directors can be jointly liable for fraudulent misrepresentations, travel restrictions may be imposed, and personal bankruptcy or veil-piercing is available against the beneficial owner who orchestrated the evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an SCSp as a bare invoice vessel for an auto-parts online retail business managed entirely from another jurisdiction, with no employees, decision-making, stock or local risk in Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Luxembourg tax administration may reclassify all profit as taxable in the real management jurisdiction, deny treaty benefits under the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test, disallow cost deductions, impose 10% to 50% penalties, and apply 15% withholding on deemed distributions if the arrangement is treated as non-transparent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner risk personal liability for repayment of taxes, interest and penalties if the shell arrangement was designed to circumvent creditors or tax enforcement; passports may be confiscated in cross-border tax-fraud proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inflating purchase prices from a related parts supplier or paying excessive e-commerce platform or management fees to a related service provider in a lower-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustment to the arm's-length price under Article 56 LIR, additional assessment of corporate income tax and municipal business tax, 10% to 50% penalties, mandatory interest, and termination of intellectual property cost-sharing arrangements if the SCSp lacks substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant or directors who knowingly signed or caused the inaccurate pricing may be personally assessed for restitution if the company is dissolved or insolvent, and could be prosecuted for tax fraud leading to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML or KYC non-compliance by e-commerce payment intermediaries
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing Stripe, PayPal or card payments without maintaining adequate beneficial-owner registers, source-of-funds verification, or transaction monitoring records, especially where SCSp investors are shell companies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CSSF administrative fines under Luxembourg AML law can reach EUR 1,000,000 or 10% of turnover, plus criminal fines; the SCSp can have its payment-processing account terminated if the beneficial owners are undisclosed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Compliance officers and managing directors face disqualification, travel bans and imprisonment up to 5 years for intentional money-laundering facilitation; courts may lift the corporate veil to collect civil damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to file or non-cooperation with Luxembourg tax authorities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Ignoring the annual information return, refusing to appoint a Luxembourg tax representative, or failing to respond to formal requests for transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Default assessments computed to the maximum possible tax, 10% automatic penalty and 5% per month incremental penalty up to 50%, 9.6% per annum late-payment interest, and listing in the Luxembourg debt-enforcement register preventing cross-border settlements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives may be personally liable under Article 710-13 of the Luxembourg Companies Act if the SCSp was stripped of assets before tax liabilities were satisfied; a director ban may be imposed by the criminal court.
